Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-22
Time: 15:00 UTC (58 min)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Marcus Lin (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Chavez (Velox CTO), Liam O'Connor (Velox Backend), Aisha Khan (Velox Security), Benji Park (Velox ML), Jordan Meyers (Redwood SE brief)

--- Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect) ---
Redwood quickstart credits and path to first token (TTFT). Discussion of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, security checkpoints (SOC 2, KMS/HSM, SSO), and pilot/benchmark next steps.

00:00 Marcus Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Rosa, Liam, Aisha, Benji, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'm Marcus, AE on the account, and Priya is our SE who'll help with the benchmarks and technical fit.
00:18 Rosa Chavez: Hi thanks, I'm Rosa, CTO at Velox, we're evaluating options to add LLM features to our docs search and customer support triage. We're leaning PLG first but need to understand security bar.
00:34 Liam O'Connor: Hey all, Liam, running backend infra, curious about latency and cost at scale.
00:40 Aisha Khan: Hi, security, looking at data residency, encryption, audit logs, and integration with our KMS.
00:46 Marcus Lin: Great. Agenda — walk through the self-serve quickstart path (free credits / TTFT), cover hosting choices (hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, private VPC/on-prem), then questions and next steps.
01:05 Priya Patel: I'll jump into the performance notes — typical TTFT for a simple generation call is minutes if you use our quickstart flow, and we give free credits for initial testing. But for a production SLA you'll want to consider dedicated or private.
01:22 Benji Park: Quick question — how do credits map to token usage? Do you give sample cost estimates?
01:28 Marcus Lin: Yes we provide cost per 1k tokens estimates per model profile; the free credits are X credits mapped to roughly Y tokens depending on model. We'll send a pricing sheet.
01:47 Rosa Chavez: Can you explain the difference between Hosted and Dedicated in plain terms? We want predictable latency but not necessarily manage infra ourselves.
01:55 Priya Patel: Sure. Hosted is our standard API — quickest TTFT, manage keys through our console. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput and capacity) and a private tenancy in our infra. Private/VPC is when you need customer-managed networking or on-prem. You'll keep control of keys and networking for VPC/private.
02:18 Marcus Lin: Important tradeoff: Hosted gets you fastest time to first token and easiest PLG path; Dedicated lowers variability and gives predictable unit economics at steady-state; Private is for strict compliance/regulatory where you need full network isolation.
02:35 Liam O'Connor: What's the route for pilot? Free credits to start on Hosted, then if things look good we move to dedicated pilot?
02:42 Marcus Lin: Exactly. Most teams start on Hosted with our quickstart credits, implement integration, run a small benchmark — if predictable SLOs and throughput are required we propose a Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity.
03:07 Aisha Khan: On security, do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM and SSO (SAML)? We need to ensure keys never leave our control for certain workflows.
03:15 Priya Patel: Yes — for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM; Dedicated supports KMS integrations depending on contract. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported in the console. We also emit audit logs for requests and role changes.
03:36 Rosa Chavez: Are audit logs real-time? We need consistent retention for compliance.
03:40 Priya Patel: Logs are streamed to the console and can be pushed to your SIEM via our logging hooks — retention can be configured per enterprise package. We'll share our security doc.
03:58 Benji Park: From an engineering standpoint, we care about latency percentiles. Do you have pre-validated perf numbers for common sequence lengths?
04:06 Priya Patel: We publish model performance profiles — e.g., gpt-like 2k prompt, 512 tokens generation, P95 latency on a hosted route is X ms (note: placeholder). For Dedicated we can provide tighter numbers since you get reserved GPU pools. Also we do KV cache and prefix caching to lower RT after repeated calls.
04:30 Liam O'Connor: You said KV cache — our ops folks call it K.V. cash in the notes sometimes. How transparent is that to the app?
04:38 Priya Patel: It's largely transparent; we keep the key-value cache to speed up recurrent contexts. For Private/Dedicated you can control how long entries persist. There's an API for pre-warming KV state if you want.
04:54 Rosa Chavez: Ok. On the pilot data flow — we have user queries that include PII in some cases. Do you support field-level redaction or masking server-side?
05:02 Priya Patel: We recommend client-side redaction before sending where possible. For Private deployments you have full control and can run redaction in your VPC. For Hosted we have tokenization-level retention controls and optional auto-redact features subject to configuration. We'll share the doc with exact retention policies.
05:27 Marcus Lin: Wanted to call out a common mistake: people over-batch to save cost and then see latency spikes. We'll help tune batching and model profiles for your workload — that's what Redwood Optimize is for.
05:42 Liam O'Connor: On cost, do you support quantized models or lower-cost variants?
05:46 Priya Patel: Yes — we surface model variants and quantization recommendations per workload. For Dedicated, you can pin a quantized variant to the pool. That reduces per-token GPU usage and cost.
06:05 Rosa Chavez: Who else from Redwood should we expect to engage if we move to a pilot? More SEs, solutions architects?
06:11 Marcus Lin: We'll add a Solutions Architect for pilot design and an implementation SE (Priya will lead). For legal/security we'll loop in our security contacts to share SOC2/ISO docs.
06:25 Benji Park: Rough timeline — we want a working prototype in about 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
06:30 Marcus Lin: For a Hosted quickstart using the self-serve API and credits, yes — most teams hit first token within a day and a basic prototype in 1-2 weeks. For Dedicated or Private pilot, plan for 2-4 weeks for provisioning and network setup.
06:50 Rosa Chavez: Good — so if we start now with Hosted quickstart and credits, we can validate end-to-end and then decide to upgrade to Dedicated. That matches our preference.
07:00 Liam O'Connor: Is there a way to run a small realistic benchmark to measure P95 and cost? We can provide a sample of 500 requests.
07:07 Priya Patel: Absolutely. Please send sample payloads and expected traffic profile. We'll run a benchmark on Hosted and if you want, we can replicate on a Dedicated pool to compare.
07:18 Marcus Lin: Actionable then: we'll share the pricing deck, how credits map to token estimates, and a security pack. Priya will get the benchmark scheduled — Benji, you'll send the sample prompts.
07:33 Aisha Khan: I need to review SOC2/ISO artifacts and confirm legal redaction policy. Who do we send that to?
07:40 Marcus Lin: Send to my email and I'll route to our security team. We'll attach the SOC2 poster and compliance pack.
07:46 Jordan Meyers (brief): Quick note — for private on-prem we have a small installer and playbook, it's a bit more lead time but feasible if your compliance needs require it.
07:58 Benji Park: One more thing — model evals. Can we run local evals to measure quality regressions between model versions before moving to production?
08:05 Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood has an evals workflow — you can pin prompt sets and we'll surface regressions when switching model versions. We'll share a link to the evals doc.
08:22 Rosa Chavez: Timeline check: we'll aim to decide internal stakeholders by next Monday and Benji will send sample payloads by Friday.
08:31 Marcus Lin: Great. Any other concerns?
08:34 Liam O'Connor: Only follow-up around caching behavior with long-lived sessions — we might have stateful chats. How do you handle KV cache eviction?
08:44 Priya Patel: Eviction is configurable; by default it's LRU with TTL settings. For private you can fully control TTL and evict granularity. We'll include config examples.
09:02 Rosa Chavez: Pricing question — if we go Dedicated pilot for a month, how do credits and billing interplay?
09:10 Marcus Lin: Typically Hosted free credits are consumed first; Dedicated pilot usually has a short-term reserved commit or trial credits depending on negotiation. We'll outline options in the pricing doc.
09:28 Benji Park: What's the expected P95 delta between Hosted and Dedicated? Even ballpark numbers help for capacity planning.
09:35 Priya Patel: Ballpark — Hosted P95 varies more due to multi-tenancy; Dedicated can tighten that by 20-40% depending on model and sequence length. We'll put actual numbers from our catalog for your profile in the benchmark results.
09:55 Rosa Chavez: Ok let's recap.
10:00 Marcus Lin: Recap: 1) We'll provide pricing deck and dedicated one-pager; 2) Priya will schedule benchmark and run Hosted test with your 500-sample payloads; 3) Security pack (SOC2/ISO, KMS guidance, audit log options) will be shared; 4) You (Rosa/Benji) will confirm stakeholders and send samples. Sounds right?
10:20 Rosa Chavez: Yes.
10:26 Marcus Lin: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in writing and get the benchmark scheduled.
10:33 Meeting ends.
